artifacts.summary: Corrects the three-hook enumeration (only UserPromptSubmit sends a project id), directly measures that POST /v1/cli/context ignores project= and returns no per-item attribution (closing the client-wrapper lever by test, not inference), reproduces the seed report's cross-repo false claims live inside this repo, confirms tasks 611/612 do not reach this defect, and sharpens the acceptance-criterion-5 vendor ask to name the correct endpoint.

memory_candidates.content: Sapience's three primary-session hooks are NOT uniform: SessionStart (mcp.py --briefing-text) calls GET /briefing + GET /v1/outstanding with no project/cwd parameter at all (by design -- outstanding is a cross-project aggregate); only UserPromptSubmit (sapience_cli.py hook prompt) sends project=project_of(cwd); PreToolUse sends neither. Both sapience_cli.py-backed hooks post to POST /v1/cli/context, a different endpoint from /v1/search (which sapience-retrieve.sh/sapience-remember.sh use and where source=[repo:tag] is proven to work).

Directly measured: Sapience's POST /v1/cli/context endpoint silently ignores its own project field -- a real project name and a nonexistent sentinel string produce byte-identical responses, including identical stale cross-repo facts (verified against live specs/state.json in two different repositories). The response envelope (enabled/event/level/ms/src/status/text/visible) carries no per-item source/project attribution anywhere, so a client-side wrapper has nothing to filter by. This forecloses any local (agent-editable) fix for Sapience's primary-session hook content scoping; the only lever is a vendor-side change to /v1/cli/context (honor project, or reflect it into provenance for a source= read filter).

Sapience's vendor client scripts ~/.sapience/mcp.py and ~/.sapience/sapience_cli.py self-update daily (confirmed via matching same-day mtimes and an update.log/.auto_update.json pair); their cited internal line numbers drift and must be re-read live rather than trusted from a prior report. ~/.sapience/upload.py does not carry the same self-update marker and its line numbers (e.g. _chunk()'s 'project': m['project'] assignment) have stayed stable across sessions.
